facts.text: Serve dessert when Jack-Jack fights the raccoon for a cookie.
facts.why: Jack-Jack spots a raccoon rummaging through the bins and fights it because it looks like a robber from TV. No source says a cookie is involved.
facts.fix: Serve dessert when Jack-Jack fights the raccoon in the backyard.

facts.text: Darling, the baby has eaten and the baby is asleep, so now we dine. Something light, and nobody wakes him.
facts.why: Edna never says this. Her real line about Jack-Jack is 'Your child is a polymorph. Like all babies, he has enormous potential.'
facts.fix: Your child is a polymorph. Like all babies, he has enormous potential.

fix_note.text: Your child is a polymorph. Like all babies, he has enormous potential.

facts.text: Violet's date at the Happy Platter.
facts.why: Violet's date with Tony is a movie date. No Happy Platter appears in the plot or any page opened.
Bob calls on Edna to babysit Jack-Jack, but no source shows it as an overnight stay.
The Deavors run a telecommunications company called DevTech. "Deavor Telecom" is not a name used in the film.

vibe.verdict: Right characters and the raccoon gets a nod, but the hotel layout does not match the Parrs' mansion and several notes make things up.
missing: Bob's 'No Sugar Bombs on my watch' and the Fiber-O's cereal (breakfast)
Jack-Jack's laser eyes and the potato-like monster form (the kitchen)
The Incredibile and its ejector seat jokes (Dash)
Frozone's no lifeguard on duty joke (pool)
ideas: Swap 'Pesto parmesan pinwheels' for 'Fiber-O's and Sugar Bombs' breakfast bites, a nod to Bob's cereal rule
Swap 'Tuna tartare on wonton crisps' for Everjust canapes, the party on the yacht
Swap the cue to a safer scene like 'Serve dessert when Bob finds Jack-Jack's powers in the backyard'
Change the venue from DevTech Penthouse to the Parrs' new mansion kitchen, which is where the family actually lives
